title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the neighbouring pages: this is the continuation of the 'Longue Marche' manuscript. Grothendieck works with group schemes over a base S_0 (the previous page removes the prime 3, 'S_0 - {3}'). The objects are:
- G_{ρ,σ} = D_12^* · 𝔖^+, a twisted, schematic version of the (profinite) modular or Teichmüller group;
- elements ρ and σ, apparently the elliptic torsion elements of orders 3/6 and 2/4;
- τ' = τσ;
- D_12^* (written O_12^* on the previous page), a group of units carrying characters ε_2, ε_3 and a ν-grading;
- the normalizer N_ρ of ρ, which sits in an exact sequence 1 → L_ρ → N_ρ → D_12^* → 1 (159), with χ_ρ the map to D_12^*.

On the previous page Grothendieck sets G^♮_{ρ,σ} = D_12^* · 𝔖^♮ (with 𝔖^♮ = M) and N_ρ^♮ = N_ρ ∩ G^♮_{ρ,σ}. Since N_ρ^♮ ∩ L_ρ = M ∩ L_ρ = 1 (161), N_ρ^♮ embeds into D_12^* via χ_ρ. He claims the image is D'^*_12 = {μ : ε_3(μ) = 1} (162).

This page proves the inclusion of the image in D'^*_12.
- Take a local section u = f^{-1} u_μ with f in M. The condition that u normalizes ρ reads int(f^{-1}) u_μ(ρ) = ρ^{ε_3}, where u_μ(ρ) = λ_1^ν ρ. Equivalently λ_1^ν ρ = int(f) ρ^{ε_3}.
- Reducing modulo the normal subgroup M kills both the λ_1^ν factor and the conjugation. This leaves ρ = ρ^{ε_3} in the quotient, forcing ε_3 = 1 because ρ has order > 2 there.
- Hence (163): N_ρ^♮ (which is in fact contained in the centralizer, so better written Z_ρ^♮) maps isomorphically onto D'^*_12. So N_ρ^♮ is a partial splitting, over D'^*_12, of the extension N_{ρ,σ} of D_12^* by L_ρ.

He then asks whether τ' (an element of N_ρ) normalizes this partial section N_ρ^♮.
- It suffices that τ' normalize G^♮_{ρ,σ}. Since τ' = τσ with τ ∈ G^♮_{ρ,σ}, this is equivalent to σ normalizing G^♮_{ρ,σ} = D_12^* · G^♮.
- σ normalizes G^♮ = G° because G° is distinguished (normal), so only the action of σ on the u_μ of (151) matters. The question becomes whether the commutators σ u_μ σ^{-1} u_μ^{-1} lie in G^♮.

The next page computes these commutators as ω^{ν_2}, where ω generates μ_2. So σ and τ' do NOT normalize G^♮ or N_ρ^♮. They do normalize the subgroups cut out by ε_2 = 1, and the outcome is a partial section N_ρ''' ≅ D_12^{*'''} = {ε_2 ε_3 = 1}.

Purpose: construct canonical (partial) splittings of the normalizer of a finite elliptic subgroup over the 'arithmetic' quotient D_12^*. This is the group-theoretic shadow of the elliptic (orbifold) points of M_{1,1} giving sections of the arithmetic fundamental group, i.e. a section-conjecture-type analysis for stacky points. It also determines how the order-2 and order-3 data obstruct, through ε_2 and ε_3, a splitting over all of D_12^*.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The reduction mod M tacitly uses three facts: λ_1^ν lies in M (or acts trivially mod M), M is normal in G^♮_{ρ,σ}, and the image of ρ mod M has order not dividing 2, so that ρ = ρ^{-1} is impossible. The text writes 'dans H^♮[?]', but the quotient used is not specified on this page.

The page is a working draft: several false starts are struck out (a first version of (164) N_{ρ,σ} = {1,τ'}, and 'est évident car G^♮ = G°'). Grothendieck's first instinct that σ normalizes G^♮_{ρ,σ} is refuted on the next page.

ideas.what: Kernel-free intersection N_ρ^♮ = N_ρ ∩ (D_12^*·M) maps isomorphically onto the index-2 subgroup {ε_3 = 1} of D_12^*. This gives a partial splitting of the normalizer extension 1→L_ρ→N_ρ→D_12^*→1.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the normalizer of a finite (elliptic) subgroup over the arithmetic quotient; sections attached to orbifold/elliptic points of M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps; also the later 'section conjecture for stacks' literature
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the role of finite subgroups and tangential/elliptic base points; this detailed computation appears unpublished

ideas.what: Reducing the normalizing condition int(f^{-1})u_μ(ρ) = ρ^{ε_3} modulo M to force ε_3(μ) = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Elementary computation of the image of a normalizer in an abelian quotient

ideas.what: Reducing the question of whether τ' = τσ normalizes the partial section to commutators σ u_μ σ^{-1} u_μ^{-1}, which the next page computes as ω^{ν_2} and which obstruct normalization through the character ε_2.
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction to equivariance of a partial splitting (sign character)

missed.claim: This is a fully worked, schematic (over a base S_0 with 3 removed) treatment of normalizers of the elliptic elements of the modular/Teichmüller group of type (1,1). It produces explicit index-2 and index-4 subgroups of D_12^*, cut out by ε_2 and ε_3, over which canonical splittings exist. Such a detailed group-scheme version does not seem to appear in published form, though analogous profinite results exist in the literature (Nakamura and others).
missed.quote: ainsi Z_ρ^♮ ... est une section partielle au dessus de D_12^{*'}, de l'extension N_{ρ,σ} de D_12^* par L_ρ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It documents Grothendieck's own approach to the arithmetic of the elliptic points of M_{1,1}, relevant to the section conjecture for stacky points and to Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. Mathematically it is probably subsumed by later results.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries routine computational steps within a larger unpublished construction. The global theme (splittings of normalizers of elliptic finite subgroups, an orbifold-point analogue of sections) is interesting historically, but this page itself adds no striking new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the underbrace label is λ_1^ν ρ, i.e. u_μ(ρ) = λ_1^ν ρ. The transcription's '^\nu' with a stray line break should read λ_1^ν.
Line 3: the corrupted 'H^\natural' is likely 'H^♮' or 'H' (the quotient mod M); the struck-out symbol before ρ^{ε_3} is illegible.
(163): the left side is N_ρ^♮ (= Z_ρ^♮) mapping isomorphically to γ'_{ρ,σ} = D_12^{*'}. The double-struck letter is the same group written O_12^* on the previous page.
'une section contenant pas τ'' should probably read 'une section ... par τ'' or 'normalisée par τ''. The handwriting suggests Grothendieck is asking whether the section is normalized by τ'.
Later lines: 'Est-ce que τ' normalise N_ρ^♮ ? il suffit [qu'il normalise] G^♮_{ρ,σ}'. The words 'comme il normalise' here belong to a struck draft.
The many '^\natural' renderings with line breaks are all ♮ superscripts (G^♮, N_ρ^♮, G^♮_{ρ,σ}).
